name: The AI Layer
oneLiner: Early shared model, retrieval, and evaluation infrastructure intended to keep CHNAI LAB products consistent and reviewable.
question: Can one shared AI layer keep evaluation, cost control, and safety boundaries consistent across several small products?
problem: When every product builds its own AI integration, evaluation logic, cost controls, and safety boundaries drift apart. Small teams pay that drift twice: duplicated work now, inconsistent behavior later.
targetUsers: CHNAI LAB product teams — internal infrastructure, not a public product.
whyItMatters: Shared infrastructure is where governance becomes real: one place to enforce evaluation contracts, spending limits, and the boundary between model output and permissioned actions, instead of hoping every product remembers.
exactRole: AI/ML system direction and evaluation standards.
teamContributions: Direction is mine; implementation would be shared across the studio. [OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED: Update as the team and responsibilities become concrete]
research: Studying how existing projects already handle evaluation and human approval (Kaskor's CER-first evaluation, Decision Grid's audit gates) to identify which patterns generalize into a shared contract rather than inventing infrastructure top-down.
validation: None yet — this is research-stage work. The direction is documented publicly in my profile; no cross-product reliability or cost benchmark exists, and this page does not claim one.
proposedSolution: A thin shared layer owning model access, retrieval, prompt and evaluation contracts, cost observability, and typed outputs — with product-specific business rules kept explicitly outside it.
userWorkflow: A product team declares its model use through the shared contract
Evaluation and cost tracking come with the contract instead of being reimplemented
Model outputs return typed and bounded; consequential actions stay in product code behind human approval
systemArchitecture: Intended shape: evaluation and observability as first-class infrastructure; bounded tools and typed outputs over unconstrained autonomy; explicit documentation of provider, model, data, and fallback assumptions. Candidate stack (Claude API, embeddings, Cloudflare AI Gateway, Supabase/PostgreSQL) is provisional.
methods: Extract-and-standardize rather than build-first: define one common evaluation contract, extract reusable pieces from one live project, and publish an architecture and failure-mode review before adding services.
businessValue: Lower duplicated integration cost and reviewable AI behavior across products — valuable exactly proportional to how many products exist, which is why it stays small until they do.
contractsPolicy: A shared layer concentrates provider terms-of-service obligations, data-processing commitments, and usage-policy compliance in one place — one of the clearest cases where reading the contracts is an engineering input.
dataPrivacy: The layer would see every product's prompts and retrieval data, making it the natural enforcement point for data-retention rules and for keeping personal data out of model calls that do not need it.
risks: Premature infrastructure — building a platform before enough products exist to justify it
A shared layer becomes a shared single point of failure without careful fallback design
Describing early infrastructure in production language would overstate its maturity — this page deliberately does not
humanApprovalPoints: Adopting the layer in any real product
Any external service or provider commitment
Any data-retention or logging decision involving user content
technicalDecisions: Evaluation and observability treated as first-class infrastructure rather than an afterthought
Product-specific business rules kept outside the shared model layer
Bounded tools and typed outputs preferred over unconstrained autonomous actions
Provider, model, data, and fallback assumptions documented explicitly

completedWork.text: Direction and design principles documented; evaluation patterns identified from existing projects
One common evaluation contract defined and applied to a first project

evidence.text: The direction is described in my public GitHub profile as early-stage infrastructure work; no public repository exists yet.
Design details beyond that are internal to CHNAI LAB.

results.text: No measurable results exist — this is research-stage work, and calling it anything else would be exactly the kind of claim this site refuses to make.

constraints: Depends on CHNAI LAB products maturing enough to need shared infrastructure
No public artifact exists to inspect yet
tradeoffs: Waiting for real product needs trades infrastructure elegance for evidence — deliberately
Keeping the layer thin limits what it can enforce, in exchange for not becoming a bottleneck

lessonsLearned: Infrastructure earns existence from repeated product pain, not from architectural ambition
Evaluation contracts are easier to standardize than prompts — start there
The governance value of a shared layer is an argument for building it slowly and reviewably, not quickly
nextValidation: Extract only the reusable pieces from one live project
Publish a minimal architecture and failure-mode review before adding services
